sections.description: This section introduces the patient's clinical presentation, highlighting the key features that prompted consideration of monogenic diabetes. It covers the initial symptoms, physical examination findings, family history, and how these elements combine to raise clinical suspicion for MODY rather than typical type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
subtopics: Patient demographics and presenting symptoms: hyperglycemia, glycosuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, and weight loss
Physical examination findings: BMI interpretation, absence of acanthosis nigricans, and vital signs
Family history analysis: autosomal dominant pattern of early-onset diabetes across three generations
Initial differential diagnosis: distinguishing MODY from type 1 and type 2 diabetes
Clinical clues suggesting atypical diabetes: age of onset, absence of insulin resistance features, negative autoantibodies

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Genetic Basis of HNF1A-MODY
sections.description: This section provides essential background knowledge on MODY with focus on HNF1A-MODY, explaining the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying this condition. It enables readers to understand why specific clinical features occur and how they inform both diagnosis and treatment decisions.
subtopics: Definition and epidemiology of MODY: prevalence, inheritance pattern, and diagnostic age criteria
HNF1A gene structure and function: location, protein product, and tissue expression
Role of HNF1A in pancreatic β-cell development, insulin secretion, and glucose sensing
Molecular mechanisms of β-cell dysfunction: impaired GLUT2 expression, reduced pyruvate kinase activity
Pathophysiology of glycosuria in HNF1A-MODY: SGLT2 regulation and reduced renal threshold
Genotype-phenotype correlations: DNA-binding domain mutations and disease severity

sections.description: This section details the systematic diagnostic approach, emphasizing how clinicians moved from initial presentation to definitive genetic diagnosis. It covers the laboratory investigations, interpretation of results, and integration of clinical data to differentiate MODY from other diabetes forms.
subtopics: Initial biochemical evaluation: HbA1c, fasting glucose, and oral glucose tolerance test results
Assessment of β-cell function: glucagon stimulation test and C-peptide interpretation
Autoantibody testing: GADA, IA-2A, and ZnT8 in excluding autoimmune diabetes
Role of genetic testing: next-generation sequencing panels and variant identification
ACMG guidelines for variant pathogenicity classification: criteria for novel variants
MODY probability calculators: utility and limitations in different populations
Novel HNF1A variant analysis: p.N270S characterization and evidence for pathogenicity

sections.section_title: Treatment Selection and Precision Medicine Approach
sections.description: This section explains the therapeutic decision-making process, from initial empiric treatment to precision medicine-guided management. It emphasizes how genetic diagnosis fundamentally altered the treatment approach and discusses evidence-based, gene-specific treatment options for HNF1A-MODY.
subtopics: Initial empiric treatment rationale: basal insulin, metformin, and DPP-4 inhibitor
First-line therapy for HNF1A-MODY: sulfonylureas and mechanism of enhanced insulin secretion
GLP-1 receptor agonists as alternative therapy: efficacy and hypoglycemia risk compared to sulfonylureas
Medications to avoid in HNF1A-MODY: SGLT-2 inhibitors and risks of dehydration and ketoacidosis
Transition from insulin to non-insulin therapy after genetic confirmation
Long-term maintenance regimen: metformin, DPP-4 inhibitors, and ongoing glycemic targets

sections.section_title: Outcomes, Clinical Implications, and Lessons Learned
sections.description: This section examines the treatment outcomes and broader implications of this case. It highlights the importance of genetic screening in early-onset diabetes, discusses challenges in MODY diagnosis, and emphasizes how precision medicine can transform patient care and family counseling.
subtopics: Treatment response: HbA1c reduction from 10.2% to 6.0% and long-term glycemic control
Monitoring for complications: microalbuminuria, retinopathy, and autonomic neuropathy surveillance
Family screening implications: cascade genetic testing and genetic counseling
Barriers to MODY diagnosis: clinical awareness, misdiagnosis rates, and limitations of clinical predictors
Significance of novel variant discovery: expanding the HNF1A mutation spectrum
Precision medicine in diabetes: impact of genetic diagnosis on treatment selection and patient outcomes
